relevance_rank_note: Directly tests both halves of H4 in one system: ApoE4 is retained with Apoer2 in intracellular compartments by co-IP (B1) while Apoer2 surface recycling is blocked (B2), and forcing dissociation by lowering endosomal pH reverses the block.

description: Apoer2 was immunoprecipitated from lysates of primary neurons treated with ApoE3- or ApoE4-conditioned media and blotted for ApoE; more ApoE4 than ApoE3 was retained in complex with Apoer2 in intracellular compartments, which the authors read as prolonged retention accompanying the delayed recycling.
quote: The delayed recycling of Apoer2 was also apparent by the prolonged retention of cell-derived ApoE4 compared to cell-derived ApoE3 in Apoer2-containing intracellular compartments as shown by co-immunoprecipitation of neuronal lysates
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more ApoE co-immunoprecipitated with Apoer2 from neuronal lysates)
system: Rat Sprague-Dawley primary cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; cell-derived naturally secreted minimally lipidated human ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles 5 ug/ml for 3 hr at 37 C; co-immunoprecipitation with anti-Apoer2 from RIPA lysate, immunoblot for ApoE, quantified relative to ApoE3
human_check: Fig 2E bar heights read off the image: E3 ~101%, E4 ~157% on a 'Relative ApoE levels (% to ApoE3)' axis, so the E4-vs-E3 increase is ~57%. Please confirm the bar reading. The ** sits on an explicit E3-to-E4 bracket and the legend key gives **p<0.01 with Student's t-test for panel E; n=3 is the 'three independent experiments' stated in the legend for all panels.

description: Cell surface biotinylation after Reelin-induced endocytosis in primary neurons: Apoer2 reappeared at the surface in the presence of ApoE3 but its surface level was far lower with ApoE4, i.e. recycling of the ApoE receptor was blocked more by ApoE4 than by ApoE3.
quote: While Apoer2 quickly recycled in the presence of ApoE3, its reappearance on the cell surface was greatly delayed in the presence of ApoE4
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less surface Apoer2 after Reelin-induced endocytosis)
system: Rat Sprague-Dawley primary cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; cell-derived naturally secreted minimally lipidated human ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles 5 ug/ml 30 min, then Reelin 2 ug/ml 30 min at 37 C; sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin surface biotinylation, surface/total Apoer2 by immunoblot normalised to no-ApoE control
human_check: Fig 2C Apoer2 bars read off the image: control 100, E3+R ~78, E4+R ~27 (surface/total normalised to control), so E4 is ~51 percentage points below E3. Please confirm. The two brackets run control-to-E3 (*) and control-to-E4 (***); there is NO E3-vs-E4 bracket, so no P is recorded for the contrast in this row per the inherited convention.

description: In the same surface-biotinylation panel, the other endocytic receptors assayed (Lrp1, Ldlr, insulin receptor, transferrin receptor) showed comparable surface levels with ApoE3 and ApoE4, so the ApoE4 surface-level effect did not extend to these receptors.
quote: the insulin receptor (IR) or the transferrin receptor (TfR), or that do not interact with Reelin and therefore do not undergo ligand-induced endocytosis (low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (Lrp1) and low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr)), were not significantly affected by the presence of ApoE
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in surface Lrp1, Ldlr, insulin receptor or transferrin receptor)
system: Rat Sprague-Dawley primary cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; cell-derived naturally secreted minimally lipidated human ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles 5 ug/ml 30 min, then Reelin 2 ug/ml 30 min at 37 C; sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin surface biotinylation, surface/total Lrp1, Ldlr, IR and TfR by immunoblot normalised to no-ApoE control
human_check: Against/null row: four receptors, all bars within ~100-105 of control in Fig 2C with no stars drawn on any of them, so no magnitude is defensible and the effect is qualitative. Note Lrp1 and Ldlr are LDLR-family recycling receptors, so this is a genuine negative for H4 beyond Apoer2; IR and TfR are included as the authors' non-ApoE-binding controls. The authors state 'not significantly affected' but print no P for these comparisons.

description: Dose-response of the NHE inhibitor EMD87580, which lowers endosomal pH away from the ApoE4 isoelectric point to force ApoE4 to dissociate from Apoer2: increasing EMD87580 progressively restored Apoer2 surface recycling in ApoE4-treated neurons, and ApoE3 produced a smaller but still significant impairment that the same concentration also prevented.
quote: physiological concentrations of ApoE3 (5 µg/ml) also impaired Apoer2 recycling to a small, but significant extent
summary: (APOE4 + forced dissociation via NHE inhibition) -> (surface Apoer2 restored to control); (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (larger recycling block at 0 uM drug)
system: Rat Sprague-Dawley primary cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; 1 hr pre-incubation with EMD87580 at 0, 1, 3 or 10 uM, then cell-derived human ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles 5 ug/ml and Reelin 2 ug/ml; surface biotinylation, surface/total Apoer2 normalised to control
human_check: Class 2 because the perturbation is a surrogate for A (forcing ApoE4-Apoer2 dissociation by lowering endosomal pH) with recycling measured. In Fig 4E the stars sit on individual E3 and E4 points against the Con curve at each drug concentration, not on an E3-vs-E4 bracket, so the P is ambiguous for this row's contrast; at 0 uM E3 ~82 (*) and E4 ~24 (***) against Con 100. The quote's 'significant' refers to ApoE3 vs control, not to E3 vs E4.

description: Solid-phase co-immunoprecipitation of secreted ApoE particles with the Apoer2 ectodomain fused to Fc across a 0-10 ug/ml ApoE range found ApoE3 and ApoE4 binding Apoer2 with similar affinity, with only ApoE2 binding poorly, so no isoform difference in direct binding affinity was detected in this cell-free assay.
quote: ApoE3 and ApoE4 bind Apoer2 with similar affinity, whereas ApoE2 binding to Apoer2 is poor
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no difference in binding to the Apoer2 ectodomain at neutral pH)
system: Cell-free solid-phase assay: Apoer2-Fc ectodomain from HEK293 supernatant bound to protein-G Sepharose, incubated 4 hr at 4 C with HEK293-secreted human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned media at 0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 ug/ml plus 1 mM CaCl2; bound ApoE detected by immunoblot
human_check: Against row and the key counterweight in this paper: the direct binding measurement finds NO E3-vs-E4 affinity difference, so the paper's retention effect (Fig 2D-E) is not reproduced as a difference in binding affinity here. Figure 1 image is NOT saved locally and I did not download it, so this row is from the Results text and legend only: no bar heights, stars or n were read, hence qualitative/N-A throughout. A human should open Fig 1B to check whether any isoform difference or error bars are visible and whether an n is stated in the source data.
